display.title: Episode 264: The Storyteller, Rabbi Yehudah's Breakthrough (Tu B'Shvat, Shabbos Shirah)
display.summary_short: Tu B'Shvat and Shabbos Shirah, a first-grade class leads the Shema, Rabbi Yehudah the storyteller hears of a rich man who pays for Baal Shem Tov stories, and the word 'lehadlik' at mitzvah time.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Tu B'Shvat 5747, which fell on Shabbos Shirah. Uncle Yossi explains that besides Rosh Hashanah in Tishrei there is a Rosh Hashanah for the trees, when we eat the fruits Eretz Yisroel is praised for and say Borei Pri Ha'etz and Shehecheyanu; like a tree, a person is judged by his fruits, his good deeds. He then explains the Song at the Sea read on Shabbos Shirah, and how a new song will be sung when Moshiach comes, followed by a march to 'Sheyibaneh Beis HaMikdash'. Story time continues the tale of Rabbi Yehudah, the Baal Shem Tov's storyteller: poor and starving after months of telling stories for pennies, he is fed by a kind innkeeper, Reb Avraham, who tells him of a wealthy merchant, Reb Yitzchak, who pays fortunes for Baal Shem Tov stories he has never heard. In between, a first-grade class from a Boro Park girls' school leads the Shema. The mailbox features a letter from a boy in Monsey, and mitzvah time teaches 'lehadlik': our job is to kindle the good hidden in every person we meet with Torah and mitzvos.
display.lesson: Like a tree, we are known by our fruits, our good deeds, and like a candle flame we must kindle the good in everyone we meet.
